answer: One defense is beacon-bound sequential work: each agent solves a proof-of-work puzzle keyed to a fresh public beacon plus its own public key, chained so each proof references the previous one, like a lotus stacking petals on a shared core. At ~30 minutes of commodity CPU per puzzle, 10,000 fake identities cost 5,000 CPU-hours per epoch - a real budget, not a copy-paste. Verification is instant, so honest agents echo the check cheaply while fakes burn saffron-priced compute. Limit: a funded attacker can still rent a botnet, so this raises the floor rather than making sybils impossible.
